Procedure: for every hunk that replaces one expression with another of the same type, name an input where they differ and check the body states it; for every removed isnan/isfinite/isinf line trace whether NaN still reaches the mismatch branch; for every changed comparison sense or default resolution compare with the comment above it and the commit message; for every removed sleep, wait, assert or lock (including one turned into a comment) ask whether it was on purpose; for every lowered threshold find the code whose behavior changes when a measured value crosses it and any values already observed at runtime. Ask form: 'was this intentional?', 'were we just getting lucky so far?'.
checks.disposition_reason: No existing check compares old and new behavior of a same-type expression swap; 5 rows over 5 PRs. The threshold row (3236579299) is folded in rather than left as a singleton.
checks.agent_feasibility: yes: detect same-type expression swaps, removed special-value lines, flipped comparisons, commented-out waits and lowered thresholds; naming the differing input needs reading the data structures; the observed-values question needs a runtime log.

checks.label: tests-run-at-head-before-approve
checks.name: No evidence that a test exercising the changed path ran at this head, in every build configuration it touches
checks.description: What breaks: the approval rests on reading alone. Multi-command changes under #ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS with no statement that the other build was tried (2915270383 'Did you sanity test that?'); timeout and sentinel changes with a test plan listing only clang-format (4265644124 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs'); a shared_ptr shard pushed onto two edges, so Wade asks whether multi-user runs were done (3156090573); his own practice of running the suite on the branch and pasting the ctest summary before approving (4131374395: 69 tests; 4422833076: 13 binaries). Procedure: for every changed region inside #ifdef X with an #else or #ifndef twin, require a body sentence that the opposite build was run; when the body's test plan is static only and the diff touches production constants or hardware-facing code, ask for a representative UT run; when a bot raises a high-severity path finding, ask for the run that exercises that path; with machine access, run the labelled binaries and paste the summary.
checks.disposition_reason: Check 3 asks whether an assertion executes on the gating lane; this widens the theme to whether any run happened at all, including the opposite build configuration and hardware-labelled tests CI cannot run.
checks.agent_feasibility: partial: the static part (ifdef twin untested, static-only test plan) is mechanical; the run itself needs a machine with the hardware labels.

checks.label: state-ownership-and-key-granularity
checks.name: One logical record or gated subsystem is written or called from two sites, a table key is unstable across forwards, or a classification is decided at the wrong granularity for production batching

style_observations: Volume and verdicts (corpus.json, counted): 334 reviews = 100 APPROVED, 234 COMMENTED, 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED. Only 12-15 review bodies carry text; 4 of those are 40 characters or shorter ('looks good to me'). 0 texts say 'LGTM'; 6 contain 'approve'. Conditional approvals in words: 'Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments. Also needs rebased.' (4373886636); 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs' (4265644124); 'I'm ok approving this as-is, although' (5156698046). 11 PRs got approval after 6+ top-level comments. He approves while nits stay open and never blocks on them.

Question form dominates: 115-122 of 267 texts contain a question mark, 82 end with one. Of the 239 review rows, form = question 93, statement 61, suggestion_block 45, ask 30. He states his reading and asks for confirmation: 18-19 texts end a claim with 'right?'; 10 ask whether a change was 'intentional' ('leaving enabled intentionally?', 'was this intentional?' verbatim in 3197414598, 3463061252, 3307473806, 3307459854); 4 open with 'I assume'; 11 'I think'; 10 'IMO/IMHO'. Typical openers: 'why ...?', 'can we ...?', 'should we just assert this?', 'still need this log?'.

Suggestion blocks for anything with a one-line fix: 43 texts carry a ```suggestion block (45 rows classified form=suggestion_block). 17 of the 19 typo rows are suggestion blocks; the rest are naming (2982403509, 2842854014, 2897235803), stale comments (3405930260, 3437533506, 3120684367), type widening (3437522787 and siblings) and small code edits (3029339639, 3350031805, 3350285744). A suggestion block often ends with '... right?' or 'and similarly elsewhere'.

Severity words are explicit and mild: 'nit' in 10-13 texts, 'trivial' 3, 'minor' 2, 'non-blocking' 1, 'follow-up' 3, 'pedantic' 5 as his self-label for style asks (2789826297, 2947931435, 2700506675, 2976643305, 4125818552). Hedges dominate: 'should' 30, 'would' 29, 'maybe' 15, 'seems' 16; 'please' only 6. Classification rows: normal 80, minor 74, nit 71, blocking 1 (3970590653, reader no longer waits for a concurrent writer). 'squash' once (5420005787); 'rebase' twice.
